lines.en: My four legs move me along slowly.
My long nose hangs over the grass.
My fleece sways as I go.
I walk along the fence line.
My hooves rustle through the grass.
I lower my head for tender shoots.
The grass here is soft enough.
I crowd forward after my flockmate.
My nose brushes the ground.
My brown fleece stirs in the wind.
I pause, then walk on.
A stone by the path; I step around.
Small steps, but steady ones.
I do not like running. I like walking.
Something rustles in the brush.
I turn into the thicker grass.
I stand, my nose still moving.
My mouth never stops chewing.
The sun lies warm on my fleece.
The wind bends my long nose.
A flockmate stands beside me.

lines.zh: 我把长鼻子搭在栅栏上。
lines.en: I rest my long nose on the fence rail.
Nothing is happening.
I shake my head.
This grass is a little coarse.
I drift toward the shade.
My nose is full of earth smell.
I snort and blow the flies away.
I paw at the ground.
My fleece is thick and very warm.
I blink twice, slowly.
It is peaceful here.
You stand taller than the fence.
I lift my eyes to you.
Your hands are empty.
My nose twitches twice.
Are you here to shear me?
I shift back a little.
There is a gap between us.
You do not look like a shepherd.
I tilt my head, and the nose tilts with it.
I go back to grazing.
How close do you plan to come?
I am only a brown sheep.
I cry out and back away.
A tuft of fleece came off.
I spring a few steps off.

lines.zh: 我哼得很响，往羊群里挤。
lines.en: I bleat loudly and push into the flock.
My chest heaves fast.
The flock has scattered.
I stand, my body tilted.
It hurts, and I bleat loudly.
My nose hit the ground and stayed numb.
Blood stains my fleece.
What is that? It smells good.
My nose reaches out for it.
I approach, pausing at each step.
I am tired of grass.
Give me a little.

lines.zh: 鼻子先探过去，嘴才跟上。
lines.en: The nose goes first; the mouth follows.
Stop waving it; I cannot reach.
I snap it up in one bite.
This tastes better than grass.
I follow you two steps.
My flockmate wants some too.
When it is gone, I go back.
Lower your hand a bit.
My nose touches your hand.
Another handful.
My long nose twitches and I lean back in.
I bump into your leg.
My fleece is soft, so the bump does not hurt.
I get shoved crooked.
My hooves slipped.
Move; let me go around.
We got bundled together.
I toss my head.
I blow a breath through my nose.
Steady. Back to eating.
You are crowding me.
I nuzzle my flockmate's neck.
We graze together.
Nose to nose.

lines.zh: 同一阵风里，我俩都闻得到。
lines.en: We both smell it in the same wind.
We take the same little path.
Walk slowly. Stay together.
Thick fleece. Winter is nothing.
We share this grass.
If something moves, we bunch up.
Another day, the same flock.
I lower my head and take it.
Two chews and down it goes.
This does not smell good.
I will try what fell.
This is not grass at all.
I carry it and sway.
My mouth is full.
This grinds against my teeth.
I push it back out.
I will save it to chew slowly.
I raise my head and lock all four feet.
I raise my head.
My flockmates have all stopped too.
I edge sideways.
My nose points that way.
I do not like this.
I bleat twice.
The flock presses together.
I mean to leave.
Do not come after me.
I keep watching over there.
My nose works and works.
Come closer and I retreat.
My ears turn to the sound.
I shift behind my flockmate.
The grass does not hide you.
I do not call out. I only watch.
All four legs are tense.
Any closer and I run.
I back slowly toward the fence.
I butt you with the bridge of my nose.
A hoof strikes once.
There is not much force in it.
I butt you aside and trot off.
I bleat loudly.
Do not grab my fleece.
I shift sideways.
You finally moved aside.
I do not want to fight either.
I push into the flock.
I walk out from behind the fence.
A coat of brown fleece.
My long nose comes out first.
A new shadow on the grass.
I appear slowly through the grass.

lines.zh: 这身棕毛是从地球带来的。
lines.en: This brown fleece came from Earth.
My flockmates came along.
Grass bits still cling to my brown wool.
The wind ruffles my fleece.
I lower my head and look for grass.
My fleece caught fire and I panicked.
My hooves gave on landing.
Water is at my back and I kick hard.
The boom has me spinning in place.
Something has sunk into my fleece.
This strange force makes me unsteady.
Not enough grass; I am thinning.
The thunder makes me jump in place.
There is not one blade of grass here.
